about: House recipes, batch 04 (helper sA): written by Claude in a Max-plan session, original, ai-draft. Nutrition is a per-serve estimate kept as data only.

recipes.title: Spanakorizo (Greek Spinach and Lemon Rice with Feta)
recipes.summary: Rice simmered with spinach, dill and lemon, with white beans and feta to make it a full meal.
steps: Heat the oil in a wide pot and cook the onion and spring onion for 5 minutes, then add the garlic for 1 minute.
Stir in the rice, then pour in the stock. Bring to the boil, cover and cook on low for 12 minutes.
Fold in the spinach and beans, cover and cook for 6 minutes more, until the rice is tender and the spinach has wilted.
Stir through the dill and lemon juice, season, then crumble over the feta.
notes: Swap the feta for extra olive oil and lemon to make it vegan.

recipes.title: Fasolakia Ladera (Greek Braised Green Beans and Potatoes)
recipes.summary: Green beans and potatoes slowly braised in olive oil and tomato until silky, served with feta and bread.
steps: Heat the oil in a wide pot and cook the onion for 6 minutes. Add the garlic and cook for 1 minute.
Add the beans, potatoes, tomatoes, tomato paste, oregano, water, salt and pepper.
Cover and simmer for 40 minutes, stirring now and then, until the beans and potatoes are very tender and the sauce is thick and oily.
Scatter with parsley and serve with feta and bread.
notes: Greek cooks braise these beans until they are soft, not crisp.
Leave out the feta to make it vegan.

recipes.title: Revithada (Greek Oven-Baked Chickpeas with Lemon)
recipes.summary: Chickpeas baked with onion, rosemary and plenty of olive oil until creamy and golden on top.
steps: Heat the oven to 190°C (170°C fan). Cook the onion in the oil in an ovenproof pot for 8 minutes, then add the garlic, paprika, rosemary and bay.
Add the chickpeas and stock with salt and pepper and simmer for 3 minutes, until hot.
Bake uncovered for 35 minutes, until the stock has reduced and the top is golden.
Stir in the lemon juice and parsley and serve with bread.
notes: The traditional version uses dried chickpeas baked for hours; canned makes this a weeknight dish.

recipes.title: Bryndzové Halušky (Slovak Potato Dumplings with Feta and Bacon)
recipes.summary: Soft grated-potato dumplings tossed with tangy sheep's cheese and crisp bacon, Slovakia's national dish.
steps: Mix the potato, flour, egg and salt into a thick, sticky dough.
Bring a large pot of salted water to the boil. Press or scrape small pieces of dough into the water and cook for 3 to 4 minutes, until they float. Lift out with a slotted spoon.
Fry the bacon in a dry pan for 6 minutes until crisp.
Mash the feta with the sour cream and toss through the hot dumplings. Top with bacon and chives.
notes: Food safety: cook the bacon until crisp and the dumplings until they float and are firm. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour.
Feta stands in for the traditional bryndza; leave out the bacon for a vegetarian version.

recipes.title: Mămăligă cu Brânză și Ouă (Romanian Polenta with Cheese and Eggs)
recipes.summary: Soft polenta swirled with butter and feta, topped with sour cream and a fried egg.
steps: Bring the water and salt to the boil. Whisk in the polenta in a thin stream and cook on low for 20 minutes, stirring often, until thick and pulling away from the pot.
Stir in half the butter and half the crumbled feta.
Fry the eggs in the remaining butter for 3 minutes, until the whites are set.
Spoon the polenta into bowls and top with the egg, remaining feta, sour cream and dill.
notes: Food safety: cook the eggs until the whites are set. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour.
Leftover polenta can be sliced and fried the next day.

recipes.title: Patatas a lo Pobre (Spanish Slow-Fried Potatoes with Peppers and Eggs)
recipes.summary: Potatoes, green pepper and onion slow-cooked in olive oil until soft and golden, topped with runny eggs.
steps: Heat the oil in a large deep pan over medium heat. Add the potatoes with 1 tsp salt and cook for 10 minutes, turning often.
Add the onion, capsicum and garlic and cook for 20 minutes, covered, stirring every few minutes, until the potatoes are tender and golden.
Stir through the paprika. Push the potato aside and fry the eggs in the pan for 3 minutes, until the whites are set.
Scatter with parsley and serve.
notes: Food safety: cook the eggs until the whites are set. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour.
Add a few slices of jamón if you like.

recipes.title: Loubia (Moroccan White Bean Stew with Paprika and Cumin)
recipes.summary: Tender white beans in a garlicky tomato sauce spiced with paprika and cumin, finished with coriander.
steps: Heat the oil in a wide pot and cook the onion for 6 minutes, then add the garlic, paprika, cumin and chilli for 1 minute.
Add the tomatoes and cook for 5 minutes until thick.
Add the beans and stock and simmer for 15 minutes, until the sauce is rich and clinging to the beans.
Stir in the herbs and lemon juice. Serve with bread or rice.
notes: A vegan one-pot dinner that keeps well and tastes better the next day.

recipes.title: Fatayer bi Sabanekh (Lebanese Spinach Pies)
recipes.summary: Little triangular pies filled with spinach, onion, sumac and lemon, baked until golden.
steps: Mix the flour, yeast, sugar, 1 tsp salt, first measure of oil and water into a soft dough, knead for 5 minutes, then cover.
Squeeze the spinach very dry, then mix with the onion, sumac, lemon juice, second measure of oil, pine nuts, salt and pepper.
Heat the oven to 220°C (200°C fan). Roll the dough out thin, cut 10cm rounds, fill each with a spoonful and pinch into triangles.
Bake on lined trays for 18 to 20 minutes, until golden. Serve with yoghurt.
notes: Prep time excludes resting the dough for 40 minutes.
Vegan if you use a plant-based yoghurt.

recipes.title: Sfiha (Lebanese Open Lamb Flatbreads)
recipes.summary: Spiced lamb and tomato spread on flatbreads and baked until crisp at the edges, an easy shortcut on the classic.
steps: Heat the oven to 230°C (210°C fan). Mix the mince, onion, tomato, tomato paste, allspice, cinnamon, pomegranate molasses and salt.
Spread the mixture thinly over the flatbreads right to the edges and scatter with pine nuts.
Bake on trays for 12 to 15 minutes, until the lamb is cooked and the edges are crisp.
Top with parsley and serve with yoghurt.
notes: Food safety: lamb mince must reach 75°C throughout with no pink. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.
Serve with lemon wedges.

recipes.title: Stamppot Boerenkool (Dutch Kale Mash with Sausage)
recipes.summary: Buttery mashed potato mixed with kale and served with a browned smoked sausage and mustard.
steps: Boil the potatoes in salted water for 12 minutes. Add the kale for the last 5 minutes, then drain well.
Fry the sausages in the oil over medium heat for 12 minutes, turning, until browned and cooked through. Cook the onion in the same pan for 6 minutes.
Mash the potato and kale with the milk, butter, salt and pepper until it is mostly smooth but still green flecked.
Serve the mash with sausages, onion and mustard.
notes: Food safety: sausages must reach 75°C in the centre with no pink inside. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.

recipes.title: Köttbullar (Swedish Meatballs with Cream Sauce)
recipes.summary: Small, tender meatballs with allspice in a gravy of cream and stock, served with potatoes and lingonberry jam.
steps: Mix both minces with the breadcrumbs, milk, egg, onion, allspice, 1 tsp salt and pepper. Roll into 24 small balls.
Brown the meatballs in half the butter for 8 minutes, turning, then lift out.
Melt the remaining butter in the pan, whisk in the flour for 1 minute, then slowly whisk in the stock until smooth. Simmer for 5 minutes.
Add the cream and meatballs and simmer for 6 minutes, until cooked through. Serve with potatoes and jam.
notes: Food safety: meatballs must reach 75°C in the centre with no pink inside. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.
Cranberry sauce works in place of lingonberry.

recipes.title: Smoky Black Bean Burgers
recipes.summary: Hearty burgers of black beans, oats and smoked paprika, crisp outside and soft inside.
steps: Mash the beans roughly in a bowl, leaving some whole. Mix in the oats, onion, garlic, paprika, cumin, tomato paste and 1 tsp salt.
Shape into 4 firm patties and chill for 10 minutes if you have time.
Fry in the oil over medium heat for 5 to 6 minutes each side, until crisp and hot all the way through.
Toast the buns for 2 minutes until golden, then build with the patties, avocado, tomato and lettuce.
notes: Vegan if the buns are dairy-free.
Patties freeze well, uncooked, between sheets of baking paper.

recipes.title: Prawn Po' Boy (Louisiana Fried Prawn Sandwich)
recipes.summary: Crunchy cornmeal-coated prawns piled into soft rolls with lettuce, tomato and a spicy mayonnaise.
steps: Mix the polenta with the cajun seasoning and a pinch of salt. Dust the prawns in flour, dip in egg, then press into the polenta mix.
Heat the oil in a frying pan over medium-high heat. Fry the prawns in batches for 2 to 3 minutes each side, until golden and opaque all the way through.
Stir the mayonnaise, hot sauce and lemon juice together.
Split the rolls, spread with the sauce and fill with lettuce, tomato and prawns.
notes: Food safety: prawns must be opaque and firm all the way through. Keep raw prawns cold and refrigerate leftovers within an hour; eat within a day.
Fry in small batches so the crumb stays crisp.

recipes.title: Chivito (Uruguayan Steak Sandwich)
recipes.summary: Thin grilled beef steak in a soft roll with ham, mozzarella, a fried egg, tomato and lettuce.
steps: Season the steak. Heat the oil in a frying pan over high heat and cook the steak in two batches for 2 minutes each, until browned and cooked through.
Lay the ham and mozzarella over the steak in the pan for 1 minute so the cheese melts.
Fry the eggs in the butter in another pan for 3 minutes, until the whites are set.
Split the rolls, spread with mayonnaise and fill with lettuce, tomato, the steak stack and an egg.
notes: Food safety: cook the thin steak to at least 63°C and rest it for 3 minutes, and cook the eggs until the whites are set. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour.

recipes.title: Anticuchos de Res (Peruvian Beef Skewers)
recipes.summary: Beef marinated in aji panca, cumin and vinegar, grilled on skewers and served with potatoes and corn.

items: 700g beef sirloin steak, cut in 3cm cubes

steps: Mix the aji panca, vinegar, garlic, cumin, oregano, oil and salt. Coat the beef and marinate in the fridge for at least 1 hour. Soak 8 skewers in water.
Boil the potatoes and corn for 12 minutes until tender, then drain.
Thread the beef onto the skewers and grill or fry on high for 3 minutes each side, until browned and cooked to your liking.
Scatter with coriander and serve with the potatoes, corn and lime.
notes: Food safety: beef cubes may be served medium (63°C) but must be seared on every side. Do not reuse raw marinade. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour.
Prep time excludes marinating.

recipes.title: Mofongo with Garlic Prawns (Puerto Rican Plantain Mash)
recipes.summary: Fried green plantain mashed with garlic and olive oil, topped with garlicky prawns in a light tomato sauce.

items: 4 green plantain, peeled and cut into chunks

steps: Fry the plantain chunks in the vegetable oil over medium heat for 10 minutes, turning, until golden and tender. Drain.
Crush 4 garlic cloves with the salt and olive oil in a large mortar or bowl, add the hot plantain and mash into a coarse mound. Shape into 4 domes.
Melt the butter in a pan, cook the onion for 5 minutes, then the remaining crushed garlic. Add the passata and simmer for 4 minutes.
Add the prawns and cook for 3 minutes, until opaque and firm. Add the lime juice, spoon over the mofongo and top with coriander.
notes: Food safety: prawns must be opaque and firm all the way through. Keep raw prawns cold and refrigerate leftovers within an hour; eat within a day.
Use plantain that is firm and green.

recipes.title: Pollo en Pepitoria (Spanish Chicken in Almond and Saffron Sauce)
recipes.summary: Chicken braised in white wine and saffron, thickened with ground almonds and a hard-boiled egg yolk.
steps: Season the chicken and brown it in the oil in a wide pot for 8 minutes. Lift out.
Cook the onion in the same pot for 6 minutes, add the garlic for 1 minute, then the wine, and bubble for 2 minutes.
Return the chicken, add the stock, saffron and bay, cover and simmer for 30 minutes.

Mash the egg yolks with the ground almonds and a ladle of sauce, stir into the pot and simmer for 5 minutes until the chicken is cooked through and the sauce thickens. Top with chopped egg white and parsley.
notes: Food safety: chicken must reach 75°C in the thickest part with no pink juices. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.
Serve with rice or boiled potatoes.

recipes.title: Polpette di Melanzane (Calabrian Aubergine Meatballs in Tomato Sauce)
recipes.summary: Soft aubergine and breadcrumb balls with mint, simmered in a light tomato sauce.
steps: Prick the aubergines and roast whole at 220°C (200°C fan) for 35 minutes, until collapsed. Scoop out the flesh, drain well and chop.
Mix the flesh with the eggs, breadcrumbs, cheese, garlic, mint, salt and pepper, then shape into 16 balls.
Cook the onion in the first measure of oil for 5 minutes, add the tomatoes and simmer for 10 minutes.
Brown the balls in the second measure of oil for 6 minutes, then lower them into the sauce and simmer gently for 10 minutes. Top with basil.
notes: Serve with crusty bread.

recipes.title: Gnudi (Tuscan Spinach and Ricotta Dumplings in Sage Butter)
recipes.summary: Light spinach and ricotta dumplings poached and tossed in brown butter and sage.
steps: Squeeze the spinach very dry and chop finely. Mix with the ricotta, egg yolks, flour, grated cheese, nutmeg, salt and pepper.
Shape into 20 small balls and roll in semolina. Chill for 20 minutes if you can.
Poach in barely simmering salted water in batches for 3 to 4 minutes, until they float and feel firm.
Melt the butter with the sage over medium heat for 3 minutes until foaming and nutty. Spoon over the gnudi.
notes: Food safety: cook until the dumplings float and are hot in the centre. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour.
Prep time excludes chilling.

recipes.title: Cataplana de Peixe (Portuguese Fish and Tomato Stew)
recipes.summary: White fish, peppers and tomato steamed in a covered pan with paprika, wine and coriander.

items: 600g firm white fish fillet, cut into chunks

steps: Heat the oil in a wide pot with a lid and cook the onion and capsicum for 8 minutes. Add the garlic and paprika for 1 minute.
Add the tomatoes, wine and bay and simmer for 8 minutes.
Add the potatoes and fish, spoon the sauce over, cover and cook for 6 to 8 minutes, until the fish is opaque and flakes easily.
Scatter with coriander and serve with lemon.
notes: Food safety: cook fish until opaque and it flakes easily (63°C). Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and eat within a day.
A closed pot works if you do not own a cataplana.
